must_remember: Only transverse waves exhibit polarization; longitudinal waves cannot be polarized.
According to Brewster's law, the tangent of the polarizing angle is equal to the refractive index of the medium ($\mu = \tan i_p$).
At Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular.
Unpolarized light passing through an ideal linear polarizer has its intensity reduced by exactly half ($I = \frac{1}{2} I_0$).
Birefringent crystals like calcite split unpolarized light into an Ordinary ray (O-ray) and an Extraordinary ray (E-ray).
A quarter-wave plate introduces a phase difference of $\pi/2$ or a path difference of $\lambda/4$.
A half-wave plate introduces a phase difference of $\pi$ or a path difference of $\lambda/2$.
Optical rotation angle is directly proportional to the path length and concentration of the active solution ($\theta = S \cdot l \cdot c$).

glossary.meaning: Light in which the electric field vector is restricted to vibrate in a single fixed plane perpendicular to the direction of propagation.
The angle of incidence at which reflected light is completely plane-polarized.
A refracted ray in a birefringent crystal that obeys ordinary laws of refraction and travels with constant speed in all directions.
A refracted ray in a birefringent crystal that does not obey Snell's law and has a refractive index dependent on the angle of incidence.
The rotation of the plane of polarization produced by a solution of unit length (1 dm) and unit concentration (1 g/cm$^3$) at a specified temperature.
Law stating that the transmitted intensity of polarized light through an analyzer varies as the square of the cosine of the angle between their transmission axes ($I = I_0 \cos^2 \theta$).
